title: Con Law II
description: Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Chapters 1–6. Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech, including obscenity, child pornography, and indecency.

First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-6_Revised.pd.title: First Amendment Outline
First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-6_Revised.pd.description: Case-by-case outline of Chapters 1–6, from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, and Free Speech Coalition v. Paxton. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes the Free Exercise, speech, prior restraint, and immoral speech checklists, along with synthesis tables.

First_Amendment_Drill.html.title: First Amendment Quick Drill
First_Amendment_Drill.html.description: 264 multiple-choice questions on every case and concept in the outline. They test what each case held, hypotheticals built on its facts, and how the doctrine applies. Filter by chapter or question type, shuffle the answers, and review only the ones you missed.

First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.title: First Amendment Flowcharts
First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.description: Interactive decision charts for Chapters 1–6. A big-picture map shows how the Religion Clauses and the speech doctrines fit together, and eight charts walk through coercion, Free Exercise, the Establishment Clause and funding, the speech framework, incitement and fighting words, prior restraints, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech. Tap any box for a plain-English explanation, the cases behind it, and what to watch out for.

First_Amendment_Case_Files.html.title: First Amendment BAR style questions 1
First_Amendment_Case_Files.html.description: Bar-style application questions for Weeks 1–6 (Chapters 1–6). Each question sets out new facts, from compelled pledges and school prayer to protest livestreams, chatbot lawsuits, and age-verification laws, and asks you to apply the doctrine. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.

First_Amendment_Case_Flash_Cards.html.title: First Amendment Case Flash Cards
First_Amendment_Case_Flash_Cards.html.description: 34 flashcards, one for each main case in Chapters 1–6, from Whitney and Barnette through Paxton and Brown. Each card asks what the case held, then gives the rule, the vote, and the key reasoning. Cited cases such as Gobitis, Yoder, Zelman, and Chaplinsky appear on the card for the case that cites them. Flip each card, then mark it Got it or Revisit.

First_Amendment_Concept_Flash_Cards.html.title: First Amendment Concept Flash Cards
First_Amendment_Concept_Flash_Cards.html.description: 32 flashcards on the core concepts of Chapters 1–6. Covers the Free Exercise and speech checklists, the ways a law fails neutrality, Establishment Clause funding, RFRA, the unprotected categories, overbreadth and vagueness, prior restraints, mens rea, the Miller test, and protecting kids versus adults.

First_Amendment_Mock_Exam.html.title: First Amendment Mock Exam
First_Amendment_Mock_Exam.html.description: A timed practice exam covering everything in Chapters 1–6: 60 bar-style questions with new facts, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at two minutes a question. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

First_Amendment_Case_Repetition.html.title: First Amendment Case Repetition
First_Amendment_Case_Repetition.html.description: 349 quick questions for Chapters 1–6. 236 drill all 34 cases by their full names: name the case from its facts, its rule, or a key line, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the cases it overruled or set up. 113 more drill the core concepts and elements across 23 topics, from strict scrutiny and the ways a law fails neutrality to the Brandenburg elements, Counterman’s recklessness standard, and the Miller prongs. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.

First_Amendment_Case_Repetition_Vol_2.ht.title: First Amendment Case Repetition, Volume 2
First_Amendment_Case_Repetition_Vol_2.ht.description: 239 new questions on the same 34 cases and 23 topics as Volume 1, asked from different angles. Name each case from a new detail, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the doctrine around it, plus 45 questions on core concepts and elements. 58 application questions put the rules to new fact patterns and explain why every wrong choice is wrong. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.
